name: Perfect verb form

source.quote: Use the simple present or simple past. 'The sync failed' is clearer than 'the sync has failed'.

message: A perfect form (has done, have been, had saved) adds a time layer that the reader must work out. Strict-plain text uses simple tenses.
fix: Use the simple past or present: 'We fixed the crash', 'The sync stopped'.

flag: The team has fixed the crash on start-up.
Demo Sync has been used by small teams since 2023.
pass: The team fixed the crash on start-up.

name: Progressive verb form

source.quote: Use the simple present or simple past. 'The service runs' is clearer than 'the service is running'.

message: A progressive form (is running, was syncing) is harder to read and to translate than a simple tense, and it can blur whether the action is finished.
fix: Use the simple present or past: 'The service runs', 'The sync stopped'. To describe a state, name it: 'The service is active'.

name: Passive voice in an instruction

source.section: Strict-plain overlay > Active voice in instructions
source.quote: In an instruction, say who does what. The reader needs to know whether they act or the system does.

message: This instruction uses the passive voice without saying who acts. The reader cannot tell whether they must do it or the system does it.
fix: Name the actor: 'Select Save' (the reader acts) or 'The installer copies the files' (the system acts).

name: Should

source.quote: 'Should' leaves the reader to guess whether a step is required. Say 'must' when it is, and 'we recommend' or 'you can' when it is not.

message: 'Should' does not say whether the action is required or optional, so the reader has to guess.
fix: If the action is required, use 'must'. If it is optional, say so: 'Optional: rotate your keys every 90 days.' If it describes expected behaviour, state the behaviour: 'The service starts'.

flag: You should rotate your access keys every 90 days.

pass: You must rotate your access keys every 90 days.

name: May

source.quote: 'May' can mean permission or possibility. Say 'can' for permission, and say what happens and when for possibility.

message: 'May' can mean that the reader is allowed to do something, or that something might happen. The reader has to guess which.
fix: For permission or ability, use 'can' with the person or thing that acts: 'Admins can delete old snapshots.' For possibility, say when it happens: 'If the network is slow, the sync takes longer'.

flag: The sync may take a few minutes.
pass: Admins can delete old snapshots.
